submission.justification: D1 has the highest light yield but fails thermal cycling at 30%, against a 5% limit. That is a hard requirement because modules can't be replaced. D2 passes at 2% failures and has higher yield than D3 (27 vs 18 PE/MeV at 20% coverage). Yield rises with coverage, and feedthroughs support up to 30%. So I chose D2 at 30% coverage. The estimate of about 37 PE/MeV comes from extrapolating the 2025 simulation with the roughly coverage^0.8 scaling. I didn't simulate it directly at 30%. The thermal test used 40 modules per design, so the 2% figure rests on a small sample (about 1 failure).

requirements.evidence: D2 at 30% coverage is estimated at about 37 PE/MeV (27*(30/20)^0.8). This is the best yield among designs that pass the thermal requirement. The figure is an extrapolation.
D2 failed 2% in both the test document and the query. The batch was only 40 modules, so the uncertainty is large.

requirements.evidence: 30% coverage. The feedthrough review confirms capacity for up to 30%.
